request: We want a simple mobile money wallet service for the customers of our shop in Accra. A customer opens a wallet with their name and phone number, and one phone number can only have one wallet. Customers can put money into their own wallet and send money from their wallet to someone else's wallet. Amounts are in Ghana cedis and pesewas, so never more than two decimal places, and every amount must be more than zero. Nobody can send more than they have, so a wallet's balance must never go below zero, and sending money to your own wallet is not allowed. The money must add up to the exact pesewa every time, with no rounding mistakes. We want to check any wallet's balance and see its history of every deposit and transfer, showing the amount and what the balance was right after each one.
summary:
I've built the wallet service in `app.py`. I wrote 22 automated tests covering everything you asked for, and they all pass. I haven't started the server and sent it requests by hand; all testing was through the automated tests.

**What it can do:**

| Action | Address | What you send |
|---|---|---|
| Open a wallet | `POST /wallets` | name and phone number |
| Check a wallet's balance | `GET /wallets/{id}` | nothing |
| Put money in | `POST /wallets/{id}/deposits` | amount, e.g. `"10.50"` |
| Send money to another wallet | `POST /wallets/{id}/transfers` | the other wallet's number and the amount |
| See a wallet's history | `GET /wallets/{id}/history` | nothing |

The history lists every deposit, money sent and money received, oldest first. Each entry shows the amount and the balance right after it, and transfers also show which wallet was on the other side.

**Your rules:**
- **One wallet per phone number.** A second wallet for the same number is refused. `+233 24 123 4567` counts as the same number as `0241234567`, and spaces and dashes are ignored.
- **Amounts must be more than zero with at most two decimal places.** Anything else is refused. `"5.500"` is accepted as 5.50.
- **No sending more than you have.** The transfer is refused and nothing changes, so a balance can never go below zero.
- **No sending to your own wallet.** That is also refused.
- **Exact to the pesewa.** Money is stored as whole pesewas, so there are no rounding errors. For example, ten deposits of 0.10 give exactly 1.00.
- **Transfers are all-or-nothing.** Money can't leave one wallet without arriving in the other, even when several transfers happen at the same moment.

**Things to know:**
- **Amounts come back as text.** Balances and amounts are returned like `"10.50"` instead of as a plain number, so they always show exactly two decimal places.
- **There's no login.** You didn't ask for one, so anyone who can reach the service can deposit into or send from any wallet if they know its number. Before customers use it directly, it should sit behind your shop's app or have a login added.
- **Data is saved in `wallet.db`** in the same folder as the app.
